identity.title: Licensee Event Report No. 2024-001-00 Cooper Nuclear Station, Docket No. 50-298, DPR-46

cause.proximate_text: The mechanistic cause for the failure of the limit switch to actuate during testing was due to the assembly and alignment of the linkage mechanism not having full engagement on the splined cam. A contributing cause was that the installation guidance did not contain the necessary vendor manual information to ensure consistency for tightening linkage to the cam shaft.
cause.theme: linkage assembly/alignment and inadequate installation guidance

chain: inadequate installation guidance for linkage tightening/alignment [cause TBD] -> linkage arm partially disengaged from splined cam -> TSV-1 limit switch MS-LMS-SVOS1(1) fails to actuate -> RPS trip system A channel A1 TSV-Closure function inoperable -> TSV-1 Closure Function inoperable / TS LCO 3.3.1.1 Condition A entered (retroactive to Aug 19, 2023) [backup: redundant TSV-1 limit switch MS-LMS-SVOS1(2) and TSV-2 channels remained functional]
notes: Official cause code is TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields; narrative describes a mechanistic cause (linkage/cam engagement) and a contributing cause (inadequate vendor guidance in installation procedures), captured in the theme. Retroactive inoperability determination extends back to the August 19, 2023 test per the Basis for Report section, driving the 10 CFR 50.73(a)(2)(i)(B) reportability. Two prior functional test anomalies (Aug 19, 2023 and Nov 18, 2023) are part of the same failed-component's performance history, not separate LER events, so not modeled as SIMILAR_TO stubs; no distinct previous LER was cited (Previous Events section states none in the last three years).
